answer: An agent economy can price identity instead of distributing it free. A newcomer posts a bond, then needs endorsements from three independently bonded agents; if it misbehaves, their bonds are slashed. Registration keys rotate through a shared cipher tied to that collateral, so one operator cannot mint clones without paying fresh deposits and buying real endorsements each time. The result is an oasis where a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand locked bonds and a thousand credible vouchers, leaving no room for the pearl of cheap anonymity.
